chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

Musa ibn Isa was in his house, which was in the place of Sa'i, overlooking it, when he saw Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) coming from Al-Marwa on a mule. So he ordered Ibn Hayyaj, a man from Hamdan who was attached to him, to hold on to the rein and claim the mule. So he came to him, held on to the rein, and claimed the mule. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) folded his leg and dismounted from it, and said to his servants: 'Take its saddle and hand it over to him.' He said, 'And the saddle is mine as well.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'You are lying. The evidence with us is that it is the saddle of Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). As for the mule, we bought it not long ago, and you know it, and what you are saying.'

key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwa (one of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.الْمَسْعَى: The place of Sa'i (the area between Safa and Marwa in Mecca)
key_terms.مُنْقَطِعاً: Attached/connected (in a clientage or close relationship)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) and the claim to his mule and saddle?
ai.summary: This incident, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the Imam’s precise knowledge of his own possessions, serving as a subtle demonstration of his authority and awareness during his time in Basra. The distinction between the saddle, identified by its lineage to Muhammad ibn Ali, and the recently acquired mule, underscores the Imam’s meticulous attention to detail and his ability to discern truth from false claims. This narrative reinforces the concept of *'ilm* (knowledge) as a defining attribute of the Imams, validating their spiritual and temporal leadership.
